meta.title_plain: How a doodle of a bald kid became Avatar: The Last Airbender
meta.teaser: Two art-school friends turned a quick sketch into a four-element world.

page.title: How a doodle of a bald kid with an arrow became Avatar
page.sub: The story of Avatar: The Last Airbender
page.bigIdea: Two friends from art school took a funny sketch and kept asking "what if?" Years of building turned it into a whole world of four elements.

cards.title: Friends from art school
cards.front: Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko met at a Halloween party in 1995.
cards.back: Both studied at the Rhode Island School of Design. Bryan helped Michael paint backgrounds for his student film. Their team-up started there.
cards.tryit: Team up with a friend on one small drawing. One draws the character, one draws the background.

cards.title: A doodle gets a makeover
cards.front: Bryan's old sketch showed a bald man with an arrow on his head and a staff.
cards.back: Nickelodeon didn't want a grown-up hero. So Bryan redrew him as a boy, but kept the bald head, arrow and staff. That boy became Aang.
cards.tryit: Find an old drawing of yours. Redraw it as a kid version, keeping three details the same.

cards.title: Ideas from everywhere
cards.front: Next, Bryan drew a boy herding flying bison. Michael added an idea from a documentary.
cards.back: The documentary was about a polar expedition, which inspired the Water Tribe. They also mixed in Asian cultures, martial arts and anime.
cards.tryit: Pick two things you love, like tennis and One Piece. Mix them into one new character idea.

cards.title: Real kung fu moves
cards.front: Every bending style copies a real martial art. Expert Sifu Kisu helped design them.
cards.back: Water uses tai chi. Earth uses Hung Gar. Fire uses Northern Shaolin. Air uses Baguazhang, which is all about circles.
cards.tryit: Watch a bending scene. Is the move smooth and flowing, or strong and rooted? Copy it slowly.

cards.title: Hit, then hit again
cards.front: The show ran from 2005 to 2008: 61 episodes in three "books".
cards.back: It won a Primetime Emmy, five Annie Awards and a Peabody. In 2020 it became Netflix's No. 1 show in the US.
cards.tryit: Name the three books: Water, Earth and Fire. Guess why there's no fourth book called Air.

words.d: In Avatar, the power to control water, earth, fire or air.
A fighting or self-defence style practised as a skill, like karate.
An expert a team asks for help on one special subject.
A new story that continues after the first one ends.
A big prize given each year for the best animation.

quiz.q: Why did Bryan redraw his bald man as a boy?
opts: Nickelodeon didn't want a grown-up hero
quiz.hint: Think about who the show was made for.
quiz.why: Nickelodeon advised against a middle-aged lead, so the man became the boy Aang.

quiz.q: Which real martial art is airbending based on?
quiz.hint: Air nomads move in circles and dodge. Look at card 4.
quiz.why: Baguazhang uses circular, dodging moves, which fit light and swirling air.

quiz.q: Where did the creators first meet?
opts: At a Halloween party at art school
quiz.hint: It was years before they worked on any TV show.
quiz.why: They met at a Halloween party in 1995 while studying at the Rhode Island School of Design.

quiz.q: What happened when Avatar came to Netflix in 2020?
opts: It became the most popular show on US Netflix
It was turned into a game
quiz.hint: Old shows can find a new audience.
quiz.why: Within its first week on Netflix it became the most popular show in the US.

page.think: Avatar began as a doodle that got changed again and again. Which of your own ideas, in drawing, LEGO or games, could grow if you kept changing it?
